summary: The article profiles Community Learning Centers (CLCs) opened in late 2023 in Johannesburg, Santa Monica, Tokyo, Queenstown, London, Rio de Janeiro and Seoul. These centers offer education to people of all ages, backgrounds and means, with programs tailored to local needs, such as reentry support, lifelong learning for seniors, immigrant services, and digital learning. It argues that CLCs are bridging educational gaps and that their success is measured in transformed lives and communities, not just statistics.
one_line: Community Learning Centers opened worldwide in 2023 are widening access to education through tailored, inclusive, partnership-driven and digital programs for all ages.
key_facts: The Soweto Community Learning Center in Johannesburg, South Africa opened on October 5, 2023, founded by educational entrepreneur Naledi Mokoena and local philanthropists; over 300 community members had enrolled by October 15.

The Ocean Park Community Learning Center in Santa Monica, USA was inaugurated on September 17, 2023, and is directed by John Davis; it offers GED preparation, ESL courses and computer literacy workshops.
Ocean Park CLC's "Second Chance" initiative supports people transitioning from incarceration back into society.
Maria Rodriguez enrolled in Ocean Park CLC's entrepreneurial courses and launched her own catering business in January 2024.
The Tokyo Metropolitan Government inaugurated the Shinjuku Community Learning Center on November 2, 2023, spearheaded by community leader Hiroshi Takahashi, with an emphasis on community building.
Shinjuku CLC held a community festival on December 12, 2023, with an interactive exhibit of adult learners' craft and technical work.
The Remarkables CLC in Queenstown, New Zealand, introduced on September 25, 2023, focuses on lifelong learning; 70-year-old Douglas Taylor studies in its digital literacy program.

The East London CLC in the United Kingdom was established on September 30, 2023, in an area with many immigrant families; director Aisha Yusuf, herself an immigrant, added language support, cultural orientation workshops and legal aid.
Fifteen-year-old Amina, who migrated from Syria, excels in school thanks to tutoring and language help at East London CLC.

The Favela Educarte CLC in Rio de Janeiro launched on October 11, 2023, through a partnership of local authorities, international NGOs and the private sector, offering education plus nutrition programs and healthcare.
Carlos Henrique, a small business owner, volunteers as a mentor at Favela Educarte CLC, and his mentorship has led several teenagers to internships and employment in his business.
The Seoul Digital CLC opened on September 12, 2023, with virtual classrooms and online learning platforms for remote learning; software developer Ji-hoon teaches coding there.
